1.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Regency is the Regency of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency

5. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person who is female from infancy, adolescence, adulthood to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family parties, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court orders. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on differentiation of humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of the recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual, economic and social as well as discrimination against victims that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual, socio-economic and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit

LO acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household scope. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person

18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, coercion of unnatural or unwanted sexual relations, coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the abilities of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, assisting, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or to the family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators. 31.

Article 12

Domestic Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter d is caused by:

a. acts that neglect women within the household sphere by someone who is obligated to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to such women;
b. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under someone's control; and
c. acts committed by family members that result in pain, bruising, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

Article 33

(2) The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of related Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by the Regent.

Article 38

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, groups as well as social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business community and mass media.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:

(4)

a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence against women;

b. taking preventive action against violence against women;

c. conducting skills training for women; and

d. establishing social community institutions that handle the guidance and empowerment of women.

Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IV

PREVENTION, PROTECTION SERVICES, AND EMPOWERMENT Part One

Prevention of Violence Against Women

Article 11

(1) Sexual Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter c is caused by:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. sexual assault;
c. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and
d. coercion of sexual relations with others and/or exploitation of women for commercial purposes and other specific purposes.
(2) Coercion of sexual relations as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) letter c is excluded for persons with mental disorders or sexual disorders in marital relations.

Article 5

Women victims of acts of violence have the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions whether government or non-government.

Part Four

Special Rights for the Protection of Women

Article 24

women's empowerment in the field of

(1) The implementation of health empowerment as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter a shall be implemented by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Health affairs.

(2) Forms of empowerment in the health field as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of health services in order to undergo a healthy, safe reproductive and sexual life, and free from coercion and/or violence.

(3) Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) include:

a. Health services for the period before pregnancy, pregnancy, childbirth and after delivery;
b. Pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health;
c. Reproductive health services; and
d. Services and provision of adequate lactation rooms at every Regional government agency, public facilities and industry.
(4) Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

Article 6

(1) Women have the right to receive special protection from matters that threaten their safety and/or health.

(2) Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.

(3) Special protection as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of health services related to: a. b.

C. d. menstruation; pregnancy; childbirth; and breastfeeding

(4) Health services as referred to in paragraph (3) may be provided by parties employing female workers in accordance with health service standards.

1. Regency is the Regency of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency

5. Regional Apparatus is the auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person who is female from infancy, adolescence, adulthood to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family parties, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court orders. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on differentiation of humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of the recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual, economic and social as well as discrimination against victims that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual, socio-economic and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit

LO acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household scope. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person

18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, coercion of unnatural or unwanted sexual relations, coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the abilities of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, assisting, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or to the family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators. 31.

(4)

b. taking preventive action against violence against women;

c. conducting skills training for women; and

d. establishing social community institutions that handle the guidance and empowerment of women.

Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 12

Domestic Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter d is caused by:

a. acts that neglect women within the household sphere by someone who is obligated to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to such women;
b. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under someone's control; and
c. acts committed by family members that result in pain, bruising, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

Article 11

(1) Sexual Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter c is caused by:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. sexual assault;
c. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and
d. coercion of sexual relations with others and/or exploitation of women for commercial purposes and other specific purposes.
(2) Coercion of sexual relations as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) letter c is excluded for persons with mental disorders or sexual disorders in marital relations.

women's empowerment in the field of
